subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency targets (Finly)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finly.com>, Samira Gupta <samira.gupta@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency targets (Finly)

Hi Alex / Samira 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call so everyone has the same picture and next steps. If I miss anything, please flag.

Pain points we heard
- End-user streaming experience is choppy: partial responses arrive out-of-order or with pauses, which impacts your in-product summarization UX.
- Tail latency: current p95 for text generation is ~1.5-2.0s for short prompts (200-400 tokens) and spikes much higher under concurrency.
- Concurrency and burst needs: baseline ~150 qps with expected marketing peak bursts up to ~300 qps during hourly batch operations.
- Cost & reliability: self-hosted setup is becoming expensive to operate at scale; want predictable unit economics and SLAs for production.

Current stack (as we understand it)
- In-house endpoints running Llama-2-13B variants on GCP (a mix of N2 CPU for preprocessing & a cluster of A2 GPUs)
- Redis for short-term caching and a homegrown router for multi-region traffic

Success criteria (Finly stated)
- p95 generation latency consistently <= 500ms for interactive flows (200-400 tokens)
- Smooth streaming UX: tokens delivered in order with <=200ms inter-token jitter for streaming endpoints
- Support baseline 150 qps with consistent p95; handle bursts to 300 qps without >2x latency degradation

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with Aditya (cc'd) to validate traffic profile + sequence lengths and to scope a POC.
2) Share SLO template and discovery slides (attached).
3) If signals look good, spin up a 2-week dedicated POC focusing on streaming and p95 under concurrency.

Attachments: redwood-discovery-slides.pdf, slo-template.xlsx

Thanks  happy to coordinate times for the technical call next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finly.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency targets (Finly)

Thanks Marissa  this looks right. A few clarifications / answers from our side:

- Streaming UX: yes, we see inter-token pauses around 300-600ms in production for document summarization. The UX impact is most visible on mobile.
- Current numbers: our internal monitoring reports p95 ~1.8s for typical summarization prompts (~250 tokens). Under load (concurrency >200), p95 can go above 3s.
- Traffic profile: steady-state ~150 qps; scheduled hourly jobs hit spikes ~250-300 qps for 10-15 minute windows.
- Sequence lengths: average request ~250 tokens in, ~220 tokens out (summarization). We do have longer ad-hoc prompts up to ~800 tokens occasionally.
- Model variants: mostly Llama-2-13B quantized to int8 for cost reasons; considering a 13B-8bit and a 7B faster variant for tail requests.

I've attached the network diagram that shows our current infra (finly-network-diagram.png).

Next week I'm available Wed/Thu afternoons (PST) for the deep-dive. We'll also pull in our infra lead if Aditya wants them on the call.

Alex
Alex Chen
Head of ML Engineering, Finly

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finly.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency targets (Finly)

Alex / Marissa  thanks for the context. A few technical questions to make sure the POC targets are actionable:

1) Tokenization & sequence distribution- Can you share the tokenized length distribution (input and output) for a 7-day sample? If not available, per-prompt averages are fine.
2) KV cache reuse- Do you expect requests to reuse cached prefixes (i.e., same user conversation) or are most requests cold? This matters for whether we need to optimize for prefix caching.
3) Streaming method- Are you using chunked streaming at the application layer or relying on the model server's native streaming? How important is immediate token-by-token delivery vs per-chunk flush?
4) TLS & KMS- Any enterprise requirements for in-transit/in-rest key management (KMS/HSM) we should be aware of for the POC?
5) Exact perf targets to verify- Confirming: p95 <= 500ms for interactive flows (200-400 tokens), inter-token jitter <= 200ms, baseline 150 qps, burst to 300 qps.

Proposed POC outline (high level)- Week 0: onboarding & env access (1-2 days)- Week 1: baseline parity tests + streaming correctness (3-4 days)- Week 2: concurrency/burst stress tests, tuning, and final report (3-4 days)

For sizing, initial estimate is a small Dedicated pool (4x A10 equivalent GPUs) for realistic streaming + concurrency testing, assuming Llama-2-13B quantized variant. I'll confirm exact GPU profile after I see token distribution.

If you can share the sample traffic and also your preferred times for the kickoff, I'll schedule the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finly.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency targets (Finly)

Aditya  thanks, good questions. Answers below and attached the 7-day sample (redacted) via the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-finly-POC

1) Tokenization: average input 250 tokens, output 220 tokens. 95th percentile input ~600 tokens.
2) KV cache reuse: ~60% of requests are within-session and will benefit from prefix/KV cache reuse.
3) Streaming: we currently use chunked streaming at the app layer; immediate token-by-token delivery is preferred for the UX but we can tolerate small per-chunk flushes (~100-200ms).
4) KMS/TLS: we use GCP KMS and require TLS 1.2+. For the POC we can provision service accounts and scoped credentials.
5) Perf targets: confirmed as listed in your email.

We're okay with the proposed 2-week POC. Wed 11 Mar 2026 1:30pm PST works for the kickoff; I'll invite our infra lead and product owner.

Attachments: finly-network-diagram.png

Speak soon  Alex
